changes.new: ### При какой нагрузке запросы укладываются в SLO В [эксперименте EPD, §4.1](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/singh25d.html) для каждого запроса проверяют два условия. TTFT, время от отправки запроса до получения первого токена, должен уложиться в свой предел. TPOT, средний интервал между последующими токенами ответа, должен уложиться в другой. Запрос засчитывается только при выполнении обоих условий. Доля таких запросов среди всех отправленных называется *SLO attainment*. На рисунке горизонтальная линия стоит на 90%. Авторы называют *goodput* наибольшую входную частоту запросов, при которой эта доля не ниже 90%. ![[00 Учебник/Assets/Figures/curated/vlm-eval-2026-11-09/epd-figure5-slo.png|Шесть графиков доли запросов, выполнивших оба ограничения: три VLM, по два изображения сверху и по четыре снизу]] *Gursimran Singh et al., [Efficiently Serving Large Multimodal Models Using EPD Disaggregation](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/singh25d.html), [Figure 5, с. 6](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v267/main/assets/singh25d/singh25d.pdf#page=6), [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Исходные панели, оси и легенда извлечены из PDF без изменений.* За один прогон отправляли 100 запросов с пуассоновскими поступлениями; ответ ограничивали десятью выходными токенами. В верхнем ряду у каждого запроса два изображения, в нижнем четыре; каждое имеет разрешение 4032 × 3024. При 2 запросах/с точка EPD для MiniCPM‑V 2.6 находится выше линии 90% на верхнем графике и ниже на нижнем. Порог TTFT для этой модели различается: 1,40 с для двух изображений и 2,60 с для четырёх, при TPOT 0,04 с в обоих случаях ([Appendix E.3, Table 9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v267/main/assets/singh25d/singh25d.pdf#page=15)). Так что рисунок сравнивает соблюдение SLO каждой нагрузки, а не эффект числа изображений при одном пороге задержки. В учебном журнале ниже при 3 запросах/с 91 запрос укладывается в TTFT, 90 в TPOT, но только 84 в оба предела. При 2 запросах/с оба условия выполняют ровно 90 из 100. Эта нагрузка проходит; она и даёт goodput на проверенной сетке частот. Если в этом прогоне 100 запросов отправили и учли за 50 секунд, частота своевременных ответов составит 90 / 50 = 1,8 ответа/с. Это другое число: goodput в статье относится к входной нагрузке, а не к числу ответов, прошедших фильтр. ~~~python # Each row: both, TTFT only, TPOT only, neither. runs = {1: (94, 2, 2, 2), 2: (90, 4, 3, 3), 3: (84, 7, 6, 3)} attainment = {rate: counts[0] / sum(counts) for rate, counts in runs.items()} assert attainment == {1: .94, 2: .90, 3: .84} assert max(rate for rate, share in attainment.items() if share >= .90) == 2 assert (runs[3][0] + runs[3][1], runs[3][0] + runs[3][2]) == (91, 90) ~~~ В Figure 5 измеряют задержку, а не правильность содержания. Сервис может уложиться в оба предела, выдав неверный итог счёта. Для продукта с такой задачей нужна также [[#vlm-eval-joint-quality|совместная проверка правильности и срока]]. ## 10. changes.old: One aggregate multimodal score mixes recognition, OCR, knowledge, reasoning, grounding, and response format. A useful evaluation separates those abilities and then tests whether the answer causally depends on visual evidence.
changes.new: An image description can name a person, a bicycle, and a road sign correctly and still invent a helmet. An invoice reader can transcribe every number correctly and return a deposit instead of the amount due. The first error concerns the presence of an object; the second concerns the role of a number. A single accuracy score does not tell you which one to fix.

changes.old:
## Composition and hallucination

Winoground uses image-caption pairs with the same words and entities but different relations. It tests whether the representation preserves composition rather than a bag of concepts.

![[02 Areas/ML & DL/00 Учебник/Assets/Figures/curated/vlm-2026/cs231n-lecture16-winoground.png]]

*Stanford CS231n 2025, [Lecture 16, slide 50](https://cs231n.stanford.edu/slides/2025/lecture_16.pdf#page=50). Winoground, CREPE, and ARO examples are shown. The same-word constraint belongs to Winoground here; CREPE also substitutes words.*
changes.new: ## Composition and hallucination On the left of [Stanford CS231n, Lecture 16, slide 50](https://cs231n.stanford.edu/slides/2025/lecture_16.pdf#page=50), one image has a cup in grass and the other has grass in a cup. The captions use the same words in different orders. Recognizing both objects won't tell a model which contains the other. The adjacent CREPE and ARO examples test other kinds of compositional errors; CREPE also changes words.

changes.old: POPE probes object hallucination with absent categories sampled randomly, by dataset frequency, or by co-occurrence with present objects. It measures one failure mode, not all hallucination: attributes, relations, counts, and OCR can also be false. “Adversarial” names the co-occurrence sampling procedure, not proof that every such question is harder for every model.
changes.new: ### POPE asks about objects that may be absent POPE probes object hallucination with absent categories sampled randomly, by dataset frequency, or by co-occurrence with present objects. It measures one failure mode, not all hallucination: attributes, relations, counts, and OCR can also be false. “Adversarial” names the co-occurrence sampling procedure, not proof that every such question is harder for every model.

changes.old: ### Follow the complete latency clock
changes.new: ### Follow the complete latency clock

changes.old: ### Cache identity depends on the cached object
changes.new: ### How much load can the service handle within its SLO? The [EPD experiment, §4.1](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/singh25d.html) checks two conditions on each request. Time to first token (TTFT) runs from request submission until the user receives the first token. Time per output token (TPOT) averages the intervals from the first output token to the last. Each metric has its own limit. A request counts only if it meets both limits, and *SLO attainment* is the share of submitted requests that do. The horizontal line marks 90%. The authors define *goodput* as the highest offered request rate with at least 90% attainment. ![[00 Учебник/Assets/Figures/curated/vlm-eval-2026-11-09/epd-figure5-slo.png|Six plots of joint SLO attainment for three VLMs, with two images per request above and four below]] *Gursimran Singh et al., [Efficiently Serving Large Multimodal Models Using EPD Disaggregation](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/singh25d.html), [Figure 5, p. 6](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v267/main/assets/singh25d/singh25d.pdf#page=6), [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Original panels, axes, and legend extracted from the PDF without modification.* Each run sent 100 requests with Poisson arrivals and fixed every response at ten output tokens. The upper row uses two images per request; the lower uses four. Each image is 4032 × 3024 pixels. At two requests per second, the MiniCPM-V 2.6 EPD point is above the 90% line in the upper row and below it in the lower row. For this model, the TTFT limits are 1.40 s and 2.60 s respectively, with a 0.04 s TPOT limit in both rows ([Appendix E.3, Table 9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v267/main/assets/singh25d/singh25d.pdf#page=16)). The rows show how each workload meets its own SLO, not what adding images does at one fixed latency limit. In the illustrative log below, at three requests per second, 91 requests meet the TTFT limit and 90 meet the TPOT limit. Only 84 meet both. At two requests per second, exactly 90 out of 100 meet both, so two is the goodput over the tested rates. If those 100 requests were submitted and accounted for over 50 seconds, the rate of timely answers would instead be 90 / 50 = 1.8 responses per second. The paper's goodput is an offered load, not a count of the answers that passed the filter. ```python # Each row: both, TTFT only, TPOT only, neither. runs = {1: (94, 2, 2, 2), 2: (90, 4, 3, 3), 3: (84, 7, 6, 3)} attainment = {rate: counts[0] / sum(counts) for rate, counts in runs.items()} assert attainment == {1: .94, 2: .90, 3: .84} assert max(rate for rate, share in attainment.items() if share >= .90) == 2 assert (runs[3][0] + runs[3][1], runs[3][0] + runs[3][2]) == (91, 90) ``` Figure 5 measures timing. A service can meet both limits and still read the wrong total from an invoice. To measure that outcome, [[#vlm-eval-joint-quality|check correctness and timing together]]. ### Cache identity depends on the cached object

changes.old: An extracted total is supported by its printed region; a computed total needs both summand regions and the operation. A crop with no established connection to the answer proves neither. When evidence is unavailable, request a clearer input or human review and measure that behavior. Rejecting every request avoids wrong outputs but solves no tasks.
changes.new: ### When to answer or send the case for review An extracted total is supported by its printed region; a computed total needs both summand regions and the operation. A crop with no established connection to the answer proves neither. When evidence is unavailable, request a clearer input or human review and measure that behavior. Rejecting every request avoids wrong outputs but solves no tasks.

changes.old: Quality and efficiency should be inspected together on photos, dense documents, multiple-image prompts, and videos. The useful result is a quality–budget–latency curve with failure slices, not one average score or a gallery of successful responses.
changes.new: ### Count answers that are both correct and timely A dense document can require more processing than a photograph and still produce a wrong answer. Report the results separately for photos, dense documents, multi-image prompts, and videos. Within each workload, count how many requests satisfy both criteria.

changes.old: This artificial ten-second log yields six correct-and-timely responses/s. It is the joint metric defined here, not a reproduction of EPD's goodput. Keep all 100 requests, failures, abstentions, timeouts, and per-class latency/quality results in the denominator and report the separate numerators.
changes.new: This artificial ten-second log yields six correct and timely responses per second. Unlike [[#vlm-slo-goodput|EPD's goodput]], it counts qualifying responses per unit time rather than the maximum offered load. Keep all 100 requests in the denominator, including failures, abstentions, and timeouts. Report the correctness and timing counts separately as well as their intersection.
